blocks.tr: Konstantinopolis bin yılı aşkın bir süre Doğu Roma'nın, yani Bizans'ın başkentiydi. Şehir Asya ile Avrupa arasında, Boğaz'ın kıyısındaydı ve Haliç adında çok iyi bir limanı vardı. 15. yüzyılda imparatorluk çok küçülmüştü: geriye neredeyse sadece şehir ve çevresi kalmıştı. Çevresindeki toprakların çoğu artık Osmanlıların elindeydi.
blocks.en: For more than a thousand years, Constantinople was the capital of the Eastern Roman, or Byzantine, Empire. It stood on the Bosphorus, between Asia and Europe, with a fine natural harbour, the Golden Horn. By the 15th century the empire had shrunk to little more than the city and its surroundings, and most of the land around it was in Ottoman hands.

blocks.tr: Sultan Mehmed 1451'de ikinci kez tahta çıktı. Hedefi Konstantinopolis'ti. 1452'de Boğaz'ın en dar yerinde, Anadolu Hisarı'nın karşısında büyük bir kale yaptı: Rumeli Hisarı. Kale birkaç ayda bitti. Bu kale sayesinde Osmanlılar Karadeniz'den gelen gemileri kontrol edebiliyordu.
blocks.en: In 1451 Mehmed II came to the Ottoman throne for the second time. His goal was Constantinople. In 1452, at the narrowest point of the Bosphorus, opposite the fortress of Anadolu Hisarı, he built a great fortress, Rumeli Hisarı, which was finished within a few months. Thanks to it, the Ottomans could control the ships coming from the Black Sea.

blocks.tr: Kuşatma 6 Nisan 1453'te başladı. Şehri kara tarafından 5. yüzyıldan kalan, altı kilometreye yakın büyük surlar koruyordu. Bu surlar yüzyıllar boyunca birçok orduyu durdurmuştu. Osmanlı topları haftalarca surlara ateş etti, ama surları geçmek kolay değildi. Şehri savunan askerlerin sayısı Osmanlı ordusundan çok daha azdı.
blocks.en: The siege began on 6 April 1453. On the landward side, the city was protected by nearly six kilometres of great walls dating from the 5th century, which had stopped many armies over the centuries. For weeks the Ottoman cannons fired at them, but getting past the walls was not easy. The defenders were far fewer than the Ottoman army.

blocks.tr: Haliç'in girişinde ise büyük bir zincir vardı ve Osmanlı gemileri bu zincir yüzünden Haliç'e giremiyordu. Sultan Mehmed bir çözüm buldu: 22 Nisan'da askerler gemileri yağlı kütüklerin üzerinde çeke çeke, Galata'nın arkasındaki tepeden Haliç'e taşıdılar. Bizanslılar Osmanlı gemilerini Haliç'te gördüklerinde çok şaşırdılar.
blocks.en: The entrance to the Golden Horn, however, was closed by a great chain, and because of it the Ottoman ships could not get into the harbour. Mehmed found a way round it: on 22 April his men hauled ships on greased logs over the hill behind Galata and down into the Golden Horn. When the Byzantines saw Ottoman ships inside the Golden Horn, they were stunned.

blocks.tr: Son saldırı 29 Mayıs sabahı başladı. Osmanlı askerleri surları geçer geçmez şehre girdiler. Son imparator Konstantinos savaşta öldü, ama son anlarını kimse kesin olarak bilmiyor. Askerler şehri yağmaladı; kaynaklar yağmanın süresi hakkında farklı şeyler söylüyor. Sultan Mehmed şehre girdiğinde Ayasofya'ya gitti ve kiliseyi camiye çevirdi.
blocks.en: The final assault began on the morning of 29 May. As soon as the Ottoman soldiers were past the walls, they poured into the city. The last emperor, Constantine XI, died in the fighting, but no one knows for certain how. The soldiers plundered the city; the sources disagree about how long the plundering lasted. When Mehmed entered the city, he went to Hagia Sophia and turned the church into a mosque.

blocks.tr: Sultan Mehmed o sırada yirmi bir yaşındaydı. Bu zaferden sonra ona “Fatih”, yani “fetheden” dediler. Başkentini Edirne'den İstanbul'a taşıdı ve şehre yeniden hayat vermek için çalıştı: onun emriyle şehre Müslüman, Hristiyan ve Yahudi aileler geldi. Kuşatmadan önce kaçan Rumlara evlerini geri verdi ve Ortodoks kilisesinin başına yeni bir patrik getirdi: Gennadios. Fatih Camii'nin ve Topkapı Sarayı'nın hikâyesi de onunla başlıyor.
blocks.en: Mehmed was twenty-one at the time. After this victory people called him Fatih, “the Conqueror”. He moved his capital from Edirne to Istanbul and set about bringing the city back to life: at his order, Muslim, Christian and Jewish families came to settle there. He gave their houses back to Greeks who had fled before the siege, and put a new patriarch, Gennadios, at the head of the Orthodox Church. The story of the Fatih Mosque and of Topkapı Palace also begins with him.

blocks.tr: Bu olayın Türkçedeki adı “İstanbul'un Fethi”; Yunancada ve birçok Batı dilinde ise “Konstantinopolis'in düşüşü” diyorlar. Birçok tarihçi 1453'ü Orta Çağ'ın sonu olarak görüyor. Şehirden kaçan bazı Bizanslı bilginler İtalya'ya gittiler ve yanlarında eski Yunanca kitaplar götürdüler. İstanbul ise 1923'e kadar Osmanlıların başkenti olarak kaldı.
blocks.en: In Turkish the event is called “the Conquest of Istanbul”; in Greek and in many Western languages, “the fall of Constantinople”. Many historians see 1453 as the end of the Middle Ages. Some Byzantine scholars who fled the city went to Italy, taking ancient Greek manuscripts with them. Istanbul remained the Ottoman capital until 1923.

questions.q: Why couldn't the Ottoman ships enter the Golden Horn at first?
options: A great chain closed its entrance
The Byzantine fleet was in the way
questions.explain: *Osmanlı gemileri bu zincir yüzünden Haliç'e giremiyordu*: *yüzünden*, **because of**.

questions.q: How did the Ottoman ships finally get into the Golden Horn?
options: They were hauled overland on greased logs
questions.explain: *Gemileri yağlı kütüklerin üzerinde çeke çeke … taşıdılar*: a doubled `-(y)A`, **pulling and pulling**.

sources.title: Fall of Constantinople
sources.note: 29 May 1453, after a 55-day siege; Mehmed II broke through the ancient land wall; the end of the Byzantine Empire

sources.title: Fall of Constantinople
sources.note: Siege from 6 April to 29 May 1453; the chain across the Golden Horn; ships dragged over the hill at Galata on greased logs on 22 April; Constantine XI's fate unknown; plunder promised for three days, sources differ on how long it lasted; Hagia Sophia made a mosque; Greek scholars to Italy; for many historians, the end of the Middle Ages

sources.title: Mehmed II
sources.note: Born 30 March 1432; Boğazkesen (Rumeli Hisarı) built between February and August 1452 to cut the city off from the Black Sea; siege from 6 April 1453, final assault on 29 May; resettlement of the city; Gennadios appointed patriarch

sources.title: Mehmed II
sources.note: Born 1432 in Edirne; reigned 1444–46 and 1451–81; known as Fatih, the Conqueror

sources.title: Mehmed II
sources.note: Capital moved from Edirne to Constantinople; Muslim, Christian and Jewish households resettled in the city; houses returned to Greeks who had fled; patriarchate restored with Gennadios in January 1454; Topkapı Palace and the Fatih Mosque among his buildings

sources.title: Rumeli Hisari
sources.note: Built by Mehmed II in 1452, in about four months, at the narrowest point of the Bosphorus to control shipping; also called Boğazkesen

sources.title: 1453: The Fall of Constantinople
sources.note: The boom across the harbour; ships taken overland into the Golden Horn; Constantine XI killed, his exact fate uncertain; Hagia Sophia converted into a mosque

sources.title: Walls of Constantinople
sources.note: The Theodosian land walls, built in the early 5th century, about 5.7 km long today; they repelled several sieges before 1453; part of UNESCO's Historic Areas of Istanbul since 1985
